opening.quote: Good afternoon, Tidewell Home, you're speaking with Joost. How can I help?
opening.comment: You gave your name and the company name in your first turn, as required.

verification.quote:
Agent: Okay. What's the order number?
Customer: It's 517204.
Agent: Right, that went to 14 Prinsengracht, 1015 AE Amsterdam, delivered on Tuesday.
verification.comment: Before sharing order details you should have confirmed the caller's full name as well as the order number or postcode; you only asked for the order number and then read out the address.

understanding.quote: Customer: Hi, my lamp arrived with the glass shade cracked. I'm really upset, it was a birthday present.
understanding.comment: You captured the issue clearly and did not ask the caller to repeat information they had already given.

resolution_accuracy.quote: A free replacement lamp is on its way and arrives in 2 to 4 working days. The lamp was €39.95, so please send the damaged one back with the free return label I'm emailing you now.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The replacement timeline and free return label for an item of EUR 25 or more are correct per policy.

process_compliance.quote: Agent: Can you email us a photo of the cracked shade first?
process_compliance.comment: You asked for the photo before arranging the replacement and emailed a free return label, as the damaged-item process requires.

communication.quote: Customer: Hi, my lamp arrived with the glass shade cracked. I'm really upset, it was a birthday present.
communication.comment: The caller said they were upset, and you never acknowledged it or apologised, so add an empathetic acknowledgement next time.

closing.quote: Agent: You'll get the tracking link by email tomorrow. Anything else I can help with today?
closing.comment: You confirmed the next step and asked if there was anything else, which closes the call properly.
